The Quiet Harbour

By Marina Koval · 12 March 2026

The harbour at dawn is a study in stillness. Boats rest on glassy water, their masts drawing thin lines against a sky that has not yet decided on a colour.

Fishermen arrive in ones and twos. They speak little, and when they do it is about the weather, which everyone already knows.

By seven the first engines cough into life. Gulls, who have been waiting all along, lift from the pilings in a single indignant cloud.

The market opens at eight. Crates of silver fish are stacked on ice, and the smell of salt and diesel settles over the quay.

Visitors come later, cameras ready, hoping to catch a scene that has mostly already happened.

By noon the harbour belongs to the cafes. The boats are out, the gulls are fed, and the water has settled back into its glassy patience.

It will all happen again tomorrow, in the same order, with the same small variations that nobody but the fishermen will notice.
